author: structure_momentum
note: Predicates 51-56: structure/momentum. bars[0] = reference (most recently closed) bar; index increases going back in time. Bars are [open, high, low, close, tick_volume]. These predicates read only closes/highs/lows of the first few bars; the default filler pads inert trailing indices (index 2 for the 2-bar predicates). THREE_DAY predicates read close[0..3] so all four bars are supplied explicitly and the filler is never consulted.

fixtures.rationale: A higher high in structure terms is an up-shifted bar: the whole range steps up, making BOTH a higher high and a higher low. bar1 high 100.0 / low 99.0; bar0 high 101.0 / low 99.5. high 101>100 and low 99.5>99, the range shifted up.

An outside bar makes a higher high (101>100) but ALSO a lower low (98.5<99): the range engulfed the prior bar, it did not shift up. This is expansion, not an up-shift, so it is not a structural higher high.
The range stepped DOWN: bar0 high 99.0 / low 98.0 sits entirely below bar1 high 100.0 / low 99.0. high 99<100 fails; this is the opposite of a higher high.
An inside-style bar: higher low (99.2>99.0) but a LOWER high (99.5<100.0). The bar coiled inside the prior high, so there is no new higher high; the high clause must reject it.

Isolates the high[0]>high[1] threshold with the low clause safely satisfied (99.5>99.0). bar0 high 100.5 is above bar1 high 100.0, comfortably clear of equality, so the strict > passes: expected true, inside the threshold.

Same low clause satisfied (99.4>99.0) but bar0 high 99.5 is below bar1 high 100.0, clearly under the threshold. Only the high value changed from the inside case, isolating which clause rejects: expected false, outside the threshold.

Isolates the low[0]>low[1] threshold with the high clause satisfied (101.0>100.0). bar0 low 99.5 is above bar1 low 99.0, clear of equality, so the strict > passes: expected true, inside the threshold.

High clause satisfied (101.0>100.0) but bar0 low 98.9 is below bar1 low 99.0, under the threshold by a clear margin. Only the low value moved across the threshold from the inside case: expected false, outside the threshold.

A lower low in structure terms is a down-shifted bar: the whole range steps down, making BOTH a lower low and a lower high. bar1 high 100.0 / low 99.0; bar0 high 99.5 / low 98.5. low 98.5<99 and high 99.5<100.
An outside bar makes a lower low (98.5<99) but ALSO a higher high (101>100): the range engulfed the prior bar, it did not shift down. Expansion, not a down-shift, so it is not a structural lower low.
The range stepped UP: bar0 high 101.0 / low 99.5 sits above bar1 high 100.0 / low 99.0. low 99.5>99.0 fails; this is the opposite of a lower low.
An inside-style bar: lower high (99.5<100.0) but a HIGHER low (99.2>99.0). The bar coiled inside the prior low, so there is no new lower low; the low clause must reject it.
Isolates the low[0]<low[1] threshold with the high clause satisfied (99.5<100.0). bar0 low 98.5 is below bar1 low 99.0, clear of equality, so the strict < passes: expected true, inside the threshold.

High clause satisfied (99.6<100.0) but bar0 low 99.5 is above bar1 low 99.0, over the threshold. Only the low value changed from the inside case: the low clause fails, expected false, outside the threshold.

Isolates the high[0]<high[1] threshold with the low clause satisfied (98.5<99.0). bar0 high 99.5 is below bar1 high 100.0, clear of equality, so the strict < passes: expected true, inside the threshold.

Low clause satisfied (98.5<99.0) but bar0 high 100.5 is above bar1 high 100.0, over the threshold. Only the high value moved across from the inside case: the high clause fails, expected false, outside the threshold.

Three consecutive up-closes across four bars: oldest to newest close 99.0 -> 99.5 -> 100.0 -> 100.5. Each close exceeds the one before, the definition of a three-day rise (close[0]>close[1]>close[2]>close[3]).
The middle rise is broken: closes oldest->newest are 99.0, 100.0, 99.5, 100.5, so close[1]=99.5 is NOT above close[2]=100.0. One down-close inside the sequence disqualifies a three-day rise.
The opposite sequence: closes oldest->newest 100.5, 100.0, 99.5, 99.0, a monotonic decline. close[0]=99.0 is below close[1]=99.5, so no rise exists at all.

The earliest two rises hold (99.0->99.5->100.0) but the most recent close 99.8 falls back below the prior 100.0, so close[0]>close[1] fails. The newest bar breaks the rise even though older bars rose.

Isolates the close[0]>close[1] threshold with the two older rises satisfied (99.0<99.5<100.0). bar0 close 100.05 is just above bar1 close 100.0, clear of equality, so the strict > passes: expected true, inside the threshold.

Older rises still satisfied (99.0<99.5<100.0) but bar0 close 99.95 is just below bar1 close 100.0, under the threshold. Only the newest close moved across from the inside case: expected false, outside the threshold.

Three consecutive down-closes across four bars: oldest to newest close 101.0 -> 100.5 -> 100.0 -> 99.5. Each close is below the one before, the definition of a three-day fall (close[0]<close[1]<close[2]<close[3]).
The middle fall is broken: closes oldest->newest are 101.0, 99.5, 100.0, 99.0, so close[1]=100.0 is NOT below close[2]=99.5. One up-close inside the sequence disqualifies a three-day fall.
The opposite sequence: closes oldest->newest 99.0, 99.5, 100.0, 100.5, a monotonic rise. close[0]=100.5 is above close[1]=100.0, so no fall exists at all.

The earliest two falls hold (101.0->100.5->100.0) but the most recent close 100.2 ticks back above the prior 100.0, so close[0]<close[1] fails. The newest bar breaks the fall even though older bars fell.

Isolates the close[0]<close[1] threshold with the two older falls satisfied (101.0>100.5>100.0). bar0 close 99.95 is just below bar1 close 100.0, clear of equality, so the strict < passes: expected true, inside the threshold.

Older falls still satisfied (101.0>100.5>100.0) but bar0 close 100.05 is just above bar1 close 100.0, over the threshold. Only the newest close moved across from the inside case: expected false, outside the threshold.
The reference bar closes above the entire prior bar: close 101.0 exceeds bar1 high 100.0. A close that clears the previous bar's high is a breakout close.
The reference bar closes at 99.9, still inside the prior bar's range (high 100.0). No breakout occurred: the close did not clear the previous high.

Intraday the bar traded above the prior high (high 100.5 > 100.0) but it CLOSED back at 99.8, below that high. The pattern is defined on the close, not the high, so a failed breakout must not register.
A down bar closing at 99.0, well beneath the prior high 100.0. Nowhere near a breakout close above the previous high.
close[0]=100.5 is above the prior high 100.0 by a clear margin, well clear of equality, so the strict close[0]>high[1] passes: expected true, above the threshold.
close[0]=99.5 is below the prior high 100.0, clearly under the threshold. Only the close moved down relative to the inside case: expected false, below the threshold.
The reference bar closes below the entire prior bar: close 98.5 is beneath bar1 low 99.0. A close that breaks the previous bar's low is a breakdown close.
The reference bar closes at 99.5, still inside the prior bar's range (low 99.0). No breakdown occurred: the close did not break the previous low.
Intraday the bar traded below the prior low (low 98.5 < 99.0) but it CLOSED back at 99.5, above that low. The pattern is defined on the close, not the low, so a failed breakdown must not register.
An up bar closing at 100.0, well above the prior low 99.0. Nowhere near a breakdown close below the previous low.
close[0]=98.5 is below the prior low 99.0 by a clear margin, well clear of equality, so the strict close[0]<low[1] passes: expected true, below the threshold.
close[0]=99.5 is above the prior low 99.0, clearly over the threshold. Only the close moved up relative to the inside case: expected false, above the threshold.
